cohort: 46 pregnant women with mechanical heart valve replacement who received low-dose oral anticoagulation treatment from October 2008 to October 2014 treated at West China Women's and Children's Hospital
finding: Bridging anticoagulation treatment combining oral warfarin and subcutaneous LMWH might be more effective and safer than single oral warfarin therapy for patients with mechanical heart valve replacement during the postoperative period, regardless of cesarean section type.
mod_finding: Discontinuation of warfarin therapy before selective CS might be more appropriate than application of vitamin K1, as preoperative vitamin K1 use might result in warfarin resistance.
